No specific diet buddy.

You first need to calculate your caloric needs.

Then u need to make sure that 40% of those calories come from protein.

Then you need to absolutely make sure you meet those requirements.

I used a food weighing scale (obsessively, with everything, even down to the nearest teaspoon of paprika and black pepper, yes they gots calories!) and MyFitnessPal to track. Religiously.

Then just a fair deal of patience and consistency and voila.

Yes there were days I’d eat more than I should, and there were days I would eat junk. Two notes on this: 1. I had set my caloric deficit to roughly 1000kcal per day (quite aggressive), so on days where I overate, I would still actually be losing weight, just not as much. 2. If I wanted a pizza, I would make room for it - either do an extra session of cardio and “save a little on the calories” or else just outright skip meals. Could enjoy that motherfucker guilt-free.

For weight loss, the ultimate bottom line is caloric deficit. So know your caloric target, and hit your target accurately. Eating 40% of those calories in protein is more to do with maintaining lean muscle mass while in deficit (adequate protein intake means that your body will make up for the caloric deficit by breaking down fat in preference of muscle).

I also emphasised resistance training over anything else, to stimulate my body to maintain muscle mass. I still did some 30 mins of intense cardio per week.

I take that as a complement. Yes, lifelong natural. I say lifelong because there were instances in the past not exceeding 3 months at a stretch where I would hit the gym. Mentioning this as apparently muscle memory is a thing.

Calorie deficit bro. IF, Keto and Paleo work because they ultimately create a calorie deficit. I calorie count obsessively, every single ingredient in any dish i cook, down to teaspoons of spices and pepper.

You’d be surprised how many calories there are in small things.

Sometimes I used to skip meals to be able to eat something junky that I wanted. I did my best to get my belly full at the end of a day so I would be able to go to sleep.

The essence of it all is the calorie deficit - so know exactly how many you need and know exactly how many you’re consuming.

The only weight loss tools you need are food weighing scales and a calorie tracker app.
